```lean
isNilpotent_of_finite_tfae.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [hG : Group G] [Fintype G] :
  [Group.IsNilpotent G, NormalizerCondition G, ∀ (H : Subgroup G), IsCoatom H → H.Normal,
      ∀ (p : ℕ), Fact (Nat.Prime p) → ∀ (P : Sylow p G), (↑P).Normal,
      Nonempty (((p : { x // x ∈ (Fintype.card G).primeFactors }) → (P : Sylow (↑p) G) → ↥↑P) ≃* G)].TFAE
```
***
A finite group is nilpotent iff the normalizer condition holds, and iff all maximal groups are
normal and iff all Sylow groups are normal and iff the group is the direct product of its Sylow
groups. 
***
*import Mathlib.GroupTheory.Nilpotent*

```lean
Sylow.normalizer_sup_eq_top.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {N : Subgroup G} [N.Normal]
  [Finite (Sylow p ↥N)] (P : Sylow p ↥N) : (map N.subtype ↑P).normalizer ⊔ N = ⊤
```
***
**Frattini's Argument**: If `N` is a normal subgroup of `G`, and if `P` is a Sylow `p`-subgroup
of `N`, then `N_G(P) ⊔ N = G`.

***
The Frattini subgroup consists of "non-generating" elements in the following sense:

If a subgroup together with the Frattini subgroup generates the whole group,
then the subgroup is already the whole group.
